A3_S5_D1: ^Oren: Gather round, gather round once again!
^Oren: Last night we left the two as they journeyed around our island and the neighbors surrounding, connecting us with ships — not boats.
^Oren: Elio was a prodigy, after all. In only a week's time, he had expanded their humble ship from a capacity of five to twenty!
^Narrator: Oren has tapestries with him this time, hung up like banners behind him as he flips in between to illustrate his points.
^Noelle: (These look very well-made… are there specialised weavers on Thavmia?)
^Oren: As the two learned more of our stories about the Great Disaster, Noah decided that it may be worth reasoning with the kraken!
^Oren: After all. If creatures were just like you and I, should the Great Disaster not empathise with the loss caused by its floods?
^Noelle: Hm… but the floods rejuvenate the land, don't they?
^Amelia: Yeah. It's pretty much common knowledge that it happens for a reason.
^Narrator: The loss of life is simply a course of nature. In the grander scale of things, the flood allows us to farm without issue, scattering people across the land.
^Oren: Alas, when ideals burn bright with hope — some march their dreams onward, despite the current of the waves.
^Narrator: The next tapestry displays a stormy sea with tentacles rising out of the surface.
^Oren: Deciding that it was his only chance to test his ideals against fate, Noah and Elio built a boat capable of entering the Dark Sea.
^Oren: They recruited those who chose to support his hope. However, positive as he may seem, a seed of doubt settled in Noah.
^Oren: Was he leading his friends onto a path of no return?
^Narrator: The next tapestry shows Noah's ship, impressively detailed, sailing against the harsh winds.
^Oren: When Noah's confidence wavered, his oldest and closest friend Elio grasped his hand, met his eyes, and—
^Oren: …Told him that no matter what… He would stay by Noah's… side?
^Narrator: Before Silas could chase him offstage, Oren quickly completes the story, flipping to the last tapestry.
^Oren: Through rain and storm, the crew finally reached the Great Disaster's home!
^Oren: Noah indeed spoke to the creature. God-like in presence and power, it loomed over him and his crew who waited from afar.
^Oren: Yet in a brief moment, chaos unfolded!
^Oren: The Great Disaster roared, striking Noah’s ship down, the mast snapped in half!
^Oren: And while we may not know what began the outburst, what remains true is this.
^Oren: A battle ensued, adventurers against creature — until finally, the Great Disaster sinks.
^Narrator: The air is tense as the final illustration is shown. The kraken retreats underwater.
^Oren: …And so, there was no flood in Noah's time.
^Noelle: (Dusk never told this story at all.)
^Noelle: (Though, it makes sense… Even if Noah was from our home, we'd never know it was him who stopped the last flood.)
^Noelle: (Mother always said that it was just an oddity — a small miracle for laborers, but bringing a new challenge for farmers.)
^Noelle: (...Things will always balance out, in some way.)
^Narrator: That is at least one universal truth, in this world of waves upon waves.
A3_S5_D2: ^Chione: There you are! The calf wanted me to give you this.
^Chione: Yes! Monsteratops tend to wear these, with more decorative materials as they age.
^Chione: It's a sign of appreciation for your help.
^Narrator: After rambling a little, Chione finally remembers—
^Chione: Right! You were curious about how Thavmia prepares for the floods, weren't you?
^Chione: In the month leading up to the flood, the settlements around the base of the island gradually gather their possessions and pack them into carts.
^Chione: There's another settlement living in the mountains, you see — and as generations came to pass, they've made progress exploring the caverns around their home.
^Chione: They work year-long to maintain and expand the tunnels, so that when the time came, the island can file in and wait out the floods.
^Noelle: How would you know when to come out? And how are the caves sealed?
^Amelia: The Ichthyos and a handful of volunteers stay outside when the flood comes. There's a communication network between the inside and out.
^Chione: Yes, but those who stay outside, even if they're Ichthyos… face a pretty big risk.
^Narrator: You can imagine. Even on clear days, just a strong gust of wind could be deadly to boats off-shore.
^Chione: And this year, there's talk of the Krakenfolk joining the Ichthyos outside, since they're used to living near the waterfall, as well.
^Narrator: Chione gestures to you with a smile.
^Chione: Krakenfolk have incredible physical strength, after all. Though I didn't know just one of you could move ruin blocks!
^Noelle: Haha… I was surprised the first time, too.
^Noelle: (Maybe sometime later, I can ask for more information about the Krakenfolk, too.)
^Noelle: (It sounds like there are a lot of others like me.)
^Chione: Oh, right! Let's go chat with Silas before Oren gets into too much trouble.
^Chione: Most of it was traditional. Just that small slip-up about Noah and Elio, uh…
A3_S5_D3: ^Elder: You’re a wonderful storyteller, Oren, but you can’t just rewrite history, no matter what your… interpretation is.
^Oren: Sorry, Silas. I guess I got carried away.
^Oren: Tomorrow’s story will have zero romantic implications, promise! …But I can’t promise the people will be happy.
^Narrator: Silas sighs, hand on hip, before turning around to greet you and Chione.
^Elder: When you and Amaya asked me whether Oren could host shows when you were little, I didn't expect it to become like this.
^Elder: Cillian is going to accuse me of favouritism at this rate.
^Chione: Haha… you have to admit that Oren's got talent, though.
^Elder: That aside, I do have something I would like to bring up to you both.
^Narrator: Silas brings out an item hidden in his cloak. It's the cloth you found with Amaya!
^Elder: Amaya brought this back from the human settlement earlier. They've recovered it to a readable form.
^Amelia: “The trees in Thavmia are not quite the kinds we are used to. But where they lack buoyancy, they are incredibly easy to work with.”
^Amelia: “We'll repurpose Starword to build the base of the ship, and find new methods to craft the deck…”
^Oren: The same writing as Noah's, from other fragments we've collected over time!
^Narrator: Silas lets Oren take the artifact, analysing the muddled sketches and ink left on the paper.
^Oren: Bri is pretty good at copying handwriting…
^Amaya: I can assure you, this item is not a forgery.
^Narrator: She explains to you that the human settlement specialises in crafts and artifact preservation.
^Amaya: If you're hoping to chase after Noah's past, they're your best bet.
^Narrator: Amaya shrugs, glancing at Silas. It's clear that they have the same idea.
^Amaya: While nature isn't calculated, many things happen for a reason.
^Amaya: And even if your connection to him isn't that deep… it's only natural for a tree to wonder where its roots hide.
^Elder: In return for your help these past days, we can supply you with some wood and ore for the repairing of your ship.
^Elder: I believe Chione has already told you about our customs regarding the floods?
^I know it may be bold of me to ask…
shyerask: ^Noelle: I may investigate a bit more about the island and Noah, before deciding on my next moves.
bolderask: ^Narrator: Silas smiles, nodding at your silent question.
afterchoicea3s5: ^Elder: We'll always welcome those who'd like to join us in the mountains. So long as they are trustworthy, and willing to help.
^Amelia: Well, no one else can clear ruins like you do.
^Narrator: For now, you'll probably head to the human settlement to learn more about the last flood, like Amaya suggested.
^Elder: If you travel upwards through our forest you’ll arrive at the human village.
^Elder: They are made up of a few un-evolved bloodlines, and new faces from the last five-hundred years.
^Noelle: (So… Noah did contribute to a bit of sea travel amongst neighbors?)
^Elder: Once you arrive, you should seek someone by the name of Cillian. He is the one responsible for all affairs — something similar to my position.
^Elder: There's been this one artifact that they haven't been able to unlock, due to its strange mechanisms.
^Elder: Perhaps if you can shed some light on that, they may be more inclined to do you a favor.
^Noelle: (While I might just join in Thavmia's plans, it'd still be good to fix up my boat.)
^Noelle: (Our ships are more than just vehicles, after all…)
^Noelle: Thank you so much for your help. Truly.
^Noelle: And to Amelia, who kindly brought me here.
^Narrator: Amelia looks away, attempting to appear nonchalant.
^Amelia: Well, since you're still kind of a newcomer, I'll keep accompanying you for you.
^Amelia: Looks like we're all planning to head to the mountains once the water rises, anyways.
^Amelia: Let's start getting ready for the night. Make sure you aren't leaving behind any luggage!
A3_S5_D4: ^Noelle: (Could there be a deeper meaning to all of this?)
^Narrator: Your father has always told you that nature runs in a cycle, and all things have a reason over time.
^Noelle: (Seems like a pretty universal sentiment with those on Thavmia, too.)
^Amelia: Hey, what's with the long face?
^Narrator: Your attention snaps to the dragon, realising you had a frown plastered on your face.
^Narrator: Amelia looks around at the bustling settlement, full of Viridi and creatures winding down for the night.
^Amelia: Why don't we look around a little? We can do some shopping— or uh, browsing.
^Narrator: The realisation that neither of you have currency makes you burst into laughter.
^Noelle: Right. Tomorrow's gonna be a busy day.
^Noelle: We should turn in once we're tired.
